reviews.title: Premium Subscription SCAM
reviews.text:
I landed on this via an Instagram post. It’s a very smooth, methodical screen flow which culminated in asking me how much I wanted to pay for reports with amounts of $1, $2, and a couple of others as choices. I selected $1 and the next thing I know I’ve suddenly been charged an additional $14.99 for a premium subscription. What? 

Nowhere on any of the screens do I recall reading an explicit “YES SIGN ME UP FOR A PREMIUM SUBSCRIPTION TO YOUR SERVICE” much less agreeing to one. I emailed customer service and the response was that no refund was forthcoming due to the “Terms and Conditions.” 

A Google search of this company/app has returned several instances over the years with people having a similar issue. Breeze would do well to fix and clarify their “checkout flow” and nip this in the bud before someone else comes along and decides a class action is the only way to go. 

I’ve since filed a dispute with my bank and expect the pending $14.99 charge to be cancelled or ultimately refunded. I won’t be doing any future business with a company that engages in shady, obscure money extraction practices.

reviews.title: Warning: Breeze Mental Health App Uses Predatory Billing & Ignores Extenuating Circumstances
reviews.text:
A mental health app should understand how memory lapses, trauma, and executive dysfunction work. Breeze does not—they monetize it.
 The Reality:
 Signed up via a "childhood trauma test" and never logged back into the platform.
 Charged over $20 for an unused service.
 Contacted support immediately to cancel and request a refund, offering full documentation of mental health status and financial hardship.
 Support hid behind rigid "Terms & Conditions," refusing any grace or human discretion.
 The Takeaway: Beware of wellness apps that use vulnerable emotional states as a funnel to lock you into auto-renewals they refuse to reverse. If you deal with ADHD, trauma, depression, or brain fog, protect your wallet and steer clear of Breeze.

Title: Charged after trial, unable to cancel

I signed up for a one-week trial and was surprised to find a $29.99 charge after it ended. When I tried to cancel, I was sent in circles.

Even though I was logged into the app, the cancellation option redirected me to a website requiring a magic link. After following that link, I received a “subscription not found” message. Trying to log in directly through the website also failed, saying no account or subscription could be found.

How can I be charged for a subscription that your cancellation system cannot find? This experience makes me feel trapped in a paid subscription with no working way to cancel.

Please fix the cancellation process, cancel my subscription, and refund the $29.99 charge. Signing up should never be easier than leaving.

reviews.title: Scam + hard to cancel
reviews.text:
I would strongly caution anyone considering subscribing. 

I signed up online and then downloaded the app, and I initially didn’t even realize I had enrolled in a recurring subscription. I was charged for two months without ever using the app. I later attempted to cancel and believed I had done so successfully, only to be charged a third time.

What bothered me the most was the response from customer service. I had explained that I had never used the app, NOT ONCE, and asked only for the most recent charge to be refunded as a one-time courtesy. They refused.

I understand companies have subscription policies, but there’s also such a thing as reasonable customer service. When an account shows no usage and customer has already paid for multiple months of service they never used, refusing to refund even the most recent charge says a lot about how the company chooses to handle its customers. 

I’ve never had this kind of experience with a subscription service before. Even if the product itself was great, the way this was handled would keep me from returning or recommending it to someone else. Be cautious.

When you contact support, this is the message you get “all the important details, such as the trial terms and the subscription’s automatic transition to a monthly plan if not canceled beforehand, were shared upfront during the sign-up process to ensure full transparency. During the same checkout flow, you also selected an optional one-time add on— personal mental wellbeing guides (this step can be skipped).” 
None of this was obvious or clear, as they claim. I was using my phone and accidentally clicked one button and was charged, I’m assuming for the wellness guides that were an “optional one-time add on.” Literally had no idea that I was purchasing something until I saw a charge on my credit card account. 
Their whole business model is built on targeting people with ADHD and CPTSD, scamming them into purchasing a subscription, making it really un-obvious what you’ve “agreed” to, and then gaslighting you saying it was so clear and obvious, and not allowing you to get your money back. reviews.title: Literally stole my money
reviews.text: App is a complete scam. I’ve had to go in THREE TIMES to cancel my subscription clicking (yes I want to cancel.) EVERY TIME and it STILL not being canceled.. Not only did they take money from me after I had canceled my subscription they also proceeded to not give me a refund. This app is literally trash for that reason on top of the fact the quizzes are just garbage.. Took several test like how mom impacted your childhood and how your father impacted your childhood. The mother ones results showed my mom had a very low impact on my childhood in terms of mental trauma meanwhile a literal article that’s attached under that very quiz about how to tell if someone has mommy issues. The going off of what article says it’s clear I am deeply affected by what my mom did but the quiz said I wasn’t? There were a few other test that would say “hey you’re basically fine.” But then have attached articles that clearly say different… it’s a cute pass time app and perhaps using the journaling and all that may be helpful… but make your quizzes better and more accurate don’t have the quiz say you’re fine and then a literal article that’s says “hey these are behaviors your show if you’re deeply hurt by something.” And then you match every single one showing the quiz was completely wrong. Also give people back their money… it’s a literal scam just go to therapy.

reviews.title: Terrible customer service
reviews.text: The app itself is fine, lots of quizzes similar to other free ones you can find online. Game was fun. But the cost was outright ridiculous, $30 a month and you aren’t even allowed to screenshot results you receive, you have to essentially sent an advertisement for the app ALONG with whatever info you were actually wanting to share . Did the free trial and then was charged $30, when I saw it my understanding was that it was for the year, given the high cost. I checked “subscriptions” under my apple account and ongoing or upcoming charges for this app weren’t there. I NEVER received a reminder I was going to be charged and I honestly forgot about it, as I haven’t used the app in a month. I was very unpleasantly surprised when I received a new charge for $30 this month with no warning (which a monthly reminder is standard for most reputable apps) haven’t used the app in weeks, I immediately reached out to customer support and expressed my frustration and stress over the surprise charge. It IS a mental health app after all, so one would think they would be responsive. But I had to send literally six messages to get a response, and it was clear from my messages that I was stressed. They FINALLY responded and assured me that I would not be getting my money back, though they offered me “sparkles” or something cheesy and offensive given the lack of concern or help I was given.

reviews.title: SCAM DO NOT USE!!!

Please be careful trusting this service as I will be getting in contact with the fair trade bureau, my bank, and any other agencies necessary to ensure i get my money back.

reviews.title: Read Better Business Bureau FIRST!
reviews.text:
Should have read the Better Business Bureau reviews on this app. I deactivated my account but I still got charged. Which was weird. So I reactivated my account and removed all of my payment information that was already ‘deleted’ according to support and then got confirmation email subscription was canceled. A week later I got charged again!  So I reached out to support who first told me I never had an account,
Then told me just because I deactivated my account doesn’t mean my subscription was cancelled.
I sent a screenshot of my email then they said “oh yes you requested the cancellation after the subscription renewal” which wasn’t the case because you can clearly see it on the email date and the day the bank processed payments. They then offered a 50% refund for good faith after the stole from me. They totally dismissed my concern about privacy and how my bank was still charged after I deleted my banking account out of account. This has happened to so many. After reading online reviews I hate I didn’t read them before.

reviews.title: BEWARE
reviews.text: This app is targeting vulnerable individuals into paying for a subscription service! Beware, They trick you by asking what you’d like to pay to get access to test results, with a $1 option. You select this and within the next few questions you’re agreeing to a $15 subscription! This may not seem like much but on their end it adds up quickly, the principle of being extremely up front about what your clients are agreeing to is vital here. Instead you agree and sign up for $1 then a simple click allows them to take $15 more. Please beware because I was in a dark place when I started the trauma test and seeing that charge sent me deeper into a spiral. Please be aware that this app and its creators do not have their client’s mental health in mind they prioritize their own pockets. When I reached out to support for a refund they simply ignored my request and never responded even after stating on the email that they get back within 4 hrs. It’s been days. Do not trust this app.

reviews.title: Misleading, Predatory, and Exploitative – Do Not Download
reviews.text:
I want to warn anyone considering this app, especially those who are genuinely seeking support after experiencing trauma.
Breeze markets itself as a trauma assessment tool, but what it really is is a cleverly disguised money trap. Here is what happened to me:
First, they present what appears to be a “voluntary” donation before you can access your results. But there is nothing voluntary about it. You cannot enter $0. The minimum they force you to pay is $1.99, with no way around it.
Then, even after completing the full assessment AND paying, a second window pops up. Inside that window, they still will not release your results. They want more money. And here is the worst part: once you click into that second window, there is NO “X” to close it. There is no cancel button. You are essentially trapped into paying again with zero way out.
When I reached out to request a refund, their response was dismissive and cold: purchases are final per their Terms of Use. No accountability. No empathy.
This app targets people who are hurting, who genuinely want answers about their mental health, and it takes full advantage of that vulnerability. They also automatically enroll you into recurring payments without making that clear upfront.
This is not a wellness tool. It is a predatory subscription scheme dressed up as mental health support. I do not recommend this app to anyone.

reviews.title: Fraud and illegal practices
reviews.text:
I found out about the app through social media and found it compelling. I tried the free trial and found that like most apps these days, it was nothing like the adds. I tried to unsubscribe and got a confirmation 5 days before the end of my 7 day trial that it was cancelled. (Mind you they forced me through a website instead of in app purchase probably because of what was to transpire). 

5 days later I see a charge on my credit card for this app. I got to try see what’s going on. The app shows I’m subscribed. When I follow their process to “unsubscribe” they say I have no active subscriptions.  I reach out to support and then the gaslighting begins. They proceed to tell me it’s now cancelled but I’m not entitled to a refund because “it’s policy”. I inform them I cancelled the trial and revoked consent to be billed before the trial ended. They proceed to tell me that’s not how it works. Well PA and Federal law disagree so they can take it up with the credit card company and the state agencies for breaking the law. 

For an app that is supposedly for self improvement they ave very predatory and manipulative, not to mention straight up fraudulent.

reviews.title: Run
reviews.text:
If you want a to actually find ways to improve mental health and move forward from childhood trauma I promise there are other ways to do it than this. I didn’t spend very long at all on this app but what I gathered from taking tests and reading the material they provided. You could get this for free. Literally with a google search you could find this stuff. What I expected this app to be was a carefully thought out app created and designed by licensed therapists. That is aimed at helping people and maybe that was the idea the creator envisioned but unfortunately it’s not that. This app is a mobile game, with a music player. That lets you track how many good/bad days you have had over the past few weeks for the low price of $30 a month.

In my experience healing is based on mutual trust and understanding between ourselves and a group or ourselves and another person serving as a guide to help interpret emotions and responses. Coupled with action taken to improve our lives. I’ve never met anyone who was able to experience healing of childhood wounds through worksheets and tracking their mood.

reviews.title: Stay away from this money grabber.
reviews.text:
The marketing for this app is completely misleading. You will probably be swayed by the hope of a test result, like a childhood trauma report, or a  personality type. You will get about six paragraphs of content that has been paraphrased, rewritten, or perhaps outright plagiarized from psychology websites and blogs—it will all sound like things you have heard before.

Most egregiously, you will never get to download your “results.” The few paragraphs are it. And the test you took to buy in to the free trial is the only free content you will get as well. The rest is content you have to pay to see, disguised as “reports.” And, for access to these paid reports, you are invited to pay $9.99/month!

The free trial lasts only 3 days too, so watch out. They will place a hold on your card to grab that first monthly payment the second the clock strikes midnight. Run, don’t walk, away from this money grab disguised as help. Then you will finally feel a breeze.

reviews.title: Absolutely a joke
reviews.text:

Abusive customer support. Misleading Instagram ads. Purposely fighting you as the “customer” while telling you that they care. I’m telling you now, I’ve seen some scams in my business. This looks like a big fat one. While disputing an issue , they chose to argue and fight with me in email. Continuously and subtly accusing me of being stupid and unable to read the “subscription” policy when the refund I was after was centered around their little Instagram campaign. Refused to work with me, I had to fight them just to get 50% of what I gave them on Instagram. And $17 might not seem like a lot, but when you take their test, pay the fee, and sign up with an email and their system glitches and triggers it under another email, it’s an issue. reviews.title: SCAM do not even pay for test results they will sign you up for a subscription
reviews.text: Same as other users have reported. I did pay to see the test results. They were sketchy at best and luckily, I saw the reviews that indicate they will sign you up for the subscription do not agree to it. I tried to login to the account on the website because that’s the only way you can cancel the subscription (does not show up under Apple account subscriptions). Of course it requires a password which you do not have because downloading the app doesn’t require a password. When you fill out the password reset form it never sends you an email, I tried it about 5 times and never got an email. I finally contacted customer support and they were actually quick to respond, provided a temporary password which I was able to then go in an cancel the subscription I never signed up for. These subscription cancellation process is convoluted. Having to move through seven different screens just to get to the final boss of actually canceling your subscription. Each screen has the cancel subscription button, tiny hidden way at the bottom while it tries to get you to click on the other options of continuing your subscription, pausing  or changing to a different subscription. I am lucky that I saw these reviews, but I am still skeptical that even though I technically canceled the subscription, I never signed up for they will still try to charge me for it.

reviews.title: Tricky to cancel
reviews.text: So you’re probably saw an ad showing someone looking at trauma results with their partner and decided to download this thinking wow maybe this will help. So you take the long test to get the app started and it opens up into a platform that shows you more little quizzes, you can take. Which you can also find on Google for free. And then when you try to cancel it, it’s really tough because your password saves in your file under a name, that’s not breeze so it’s hard to determine how to login and cancel pay attention to the website that it’s saving for if you use your password filler… So that you could identify the name of the account it is actually under when you try to cancel or log back in. It won’t automatically go to fill in your Breeze app because it doesn’t recognize it. It is not labeled as breeze in any way shape or form in your password that you save on your phone. One last thing the app will tell you that you need to finish quizzes to get your free gift. Your free gift is a 20% discount off of therapy with the parent company of this app which is BetterHelp. My suggestion is if you are looking for guidance for your growth and the challenges you’re having just get the BetterHelp AP and get yourself a human therapist
